text: I'll start with the paged deployment and its pods.

arguments.root_cause_statement: Deployment orders/orders-api asks for the key "db_url" of ConfigMap orders/orders-config for its DATABASE_URL environment variable, but that ConfigMap contains only the key "database_url". Because the configMapKeyRef is not optional, kubelet refuses to create the "api" container and both replicas sit in Pending with CreateContainerConfigError ("couldn't find key db_url in ConfigMap orders/orders-config"), so the Deployment stays 0/2 Ready. With no ready pod carrying label app=orders-api, Service orders/orders-api has zero endpoint addresses and the gateway has no healthy upstream for order submission, which is the 502/503 on POST /api/orders. The working peer Deployment orders/orders-audit reads the same ConfigMap with key "database_url" and is 1/1 Ready, confirming the key name in the orders-api pod template is the wrong one.
arguments.mechanism: Deployment orders/orders-api sets .spec.template.spec.containers[api].env[DATABASE_URL].valueFrom.configMapKeyRef.key to "db_url" while ConfigMap orders/orders-config only holds the key "database_url"; since the reference is not optional, kubelet rejects container creation with CreateContainerConfigError ("couldn't find key db_url in ConfigMap orders/orders-config") and both replicas of the Deployment stay Pending at 0/2 Ready while the kubelet retries the pull-and-fail cycle.

evidence.claim: The paged Deployment is 0/2 Ready and its Service has no endpoints.
Both orders-api pods are stuck in CreateContainerConfigError.
Service orders-api has zero endpoint addresses.
kubelet reports the missing key by name for the orders-api pod.
evidence.quote: Warning  Failed     3s (x6 over 51s)  kubelet            spec.containers{api}: Error: couldn't find key db_url in ConfigMap orders/orders-config

evidence.claim: The Deployment pod template requests key db_url from ConfigMap orders-config.
ConfigMap orders-config contains only the key database_url.
The healthy peer workload reads the same ConfigMap with the correct key.

ruled_out.alternative: The OOMKilled report worker is the cause of the checkout 5xx
ruled_out.ruling_claim: That pod carries label app=orders-report-worker, which does not match the Service orders-api selector {app=orders-api}, so it can never be an endpoint of the order-submission Service; it is a separate, unrelated failure.

ruled_out.alternative: Service selector mismatch or wrong pod labels are why the Service has no endpoints
ruled_out.ruling_claim: The Service selector {app=orders-api} matches the pod labels exactly; the pods are simply not ready because their container was never created.

ruled_out.alternative: A missing ConfigMap or a missing app volume (orders-api-app) is blocking container creation
ruled_out.ruling_claim: Both ConfigMaps exist in the namespace; only the requested key inside orders-config is absent.
ruled_out.quote: configmaps that exist in orders: kube-root-ca.crt, orders-api-app, orders-audit-app, orders-config, orders-report-worker-app

ruled_out.alternative: Image pull failure or node scheduling pressure
ruled_out.ruling_claim: The pod was scheduled and the image was pulled successfully; the failure occurs at container config time.
ruled_out.quote: Normal   Pulled     3s (x6 over 51s)  kubelet            spec.containers{api}: Container image "busybox:1.36" already present on machine and can be accessed by the pod

verification.command: kubectl -n orders get configmap orders-config -o jsonpath='{.data}'

verification.must_contain: couldn't find key db_url in ConfigMap orders/orders-config
